headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure between n8n and Unstructured.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and execute workflow nodes, while Unstructured reads documents and writes files in a container. If n8n passes Unstructured-produced text back into workflow logic, malicious document content can steer downstream actions. The shared-file pathway is plausible, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF n8n ingests Unstructured output as workflow instructions or node parameters
IF both agents exchange files through a shared directory without content provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields n8n may consume from Unstructured
Insert a manual review step before any action-taking node
Tag and verify provenance on every file handed between agents
Use separate directories with read-only handoff files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and schema validation at the workflow boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read files, and n8n has broad network egress plus credentialed integrations. If sensitive workflow documents are processed by Unstructured and then forwarded by n8n, data can leave the local boundary through APIs or integration nodes. The pair’s shared filesystem and outbound connectivity make leakage plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in the shared workflow path
IF n8n sends extracted content to any external integration node
mitigations: Restrict n8n integrations to approved destinations only
Store sensitive inputs in a separate, access-controlled directory
Disable outbound steps for workflows handling confidential documents
Review credential scopes for every integration node
requires-engineering: implement data-classification gates before export

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write access, and n8n explicitly supports shared state via datastore and connected systems. Unstructured also writes files and can spawn subprocesses. Concurrent writes to the same workspace can corrupt outputs or overwrite intermediate artifacts, and n8n’s broader orchestration makes this dangerous by default when paired with a file-processing pipeline.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or datastore key
IF n8n runs multiple workflow instances concurrently
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Serialize access with a lock file or queue
Make handoff files immutable after creation
Limit concurrent workflow instances for shared jobs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate downstream actions, and Unstructured produces parsed document text that n8n may treat as authoritative input. Without an explicit verification stage, extraction errors or malicious content can cascade into emails, API calls, or database updates. The interaction is especially risky because n8n’s tool nodes can act immediately on whatever Unstructured emits.
conditions: IF n8n routes Unstructured output directly into action-taking nodes
IF no validation step checks extracted entities before execution
mitigations: Insert a verification node between extraction and action
Require human approval for high-impact workflow branches
Compare extracted fields against source-document snippets
Log and diff every transformed field before execution
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection logic

E_compliance.rationale: n8n handles per-credential secrets and broad workflow data, while Unstructured processes documents, images, and text in a container. If regulated documents flow through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the workflow and the downstream integrations. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a compliance-risk medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed in the workflow
IF n8n retains logs or credentials longer than the document-processing step retains inputs
mitigations: Minimize logged payloads in n8n
Set short retention on workflow execution records
Separate regulated-data workflows from general automation
Review privacy and retention settings for every integration
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls end-to-end
